High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko
Counsel for Applicant :- Ratnesh Kant Agnihotri,Ranjana Agnihotri

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Karunesh Singh Pawar,J.
1.Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State and perused the record.
2.It is alleged in the prosecution case that the informant met Kuldeep Kumar Gupta, present applicant and co-accused Pradeep Kumar Gupta in RBS Coaching Centre.
They allured to provide government job to the complainant on the pretext of good relations with FCI Director.
The complainant and others gave Rs.35,90,000/- to secure job in government organisation.
Forged letters were given by the applicant belonging to FCI to the victim Deepak Verma, Vikas Verma and others.

Since 2018, present applicant has been procrastinating the informant side and when the Kuldeep Kumar Gupta vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198723802/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: informant side demanded his money, the accused persons abused and threatened the informant to implicate in false case.
3.Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is the victim himself.
The applicant was cheated by the gang of Rajender Verma.

Thus, a first information report was lodged by him,
bearing crime No.131 of 2021 at police station Vikas Nagar, Lucknow against the gang member of Rajendra Verma, namely Aman Verma and Ajeet Verma.
The investigating officer sided with the informant's gang and submitted final report.
A complaint was made by the applicant to the Director General of Police and also on IGRS against Rajender Verma and his gang.
Ultimately, a Crl. Misc. W.P. No.9957 of 2022 was filed before this Court.
Still, a final report was filed in the year 2023.
A protest petition was filed by the applicant before the learned Magistrate where the Magistrate has passed strictures on the investigating officer.
It is submitted by applicant's counsel that there is nothing on record to show that the applicant has received any amount in his personal account as alleged in the first information report.
The applicant is the co-Director of RBSB Infotech Private Limited.
A petty amount of Rs.1,70,000/- shown to be received by the company has no concern with the applicant.
The applicant is not entrusted with that job.
He has a specified job which is not linked with that money.
The applicant has no criminal history.
The offence is triable by Magistrate.
The applicant is in jail since 2.8.2024.
It is further submitted that there is no possibility of the applicant of fleeing away after being released on bail or tampering with the witnesses.
In case the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail.
4.Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the aforesaid facts as argued by the learned counsel for the applicant.

5.Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the fact that the applicant has no criminal history, the offence is triable by Magistrate, earlier, a first information report was lodged by the applicant, arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, the period for which the applicant is in jail and without expressing any opinion on the merit of the case, I find it to be a fit case for enlarging the applicant on bail.
6.Let the applicant Kuldeep Kumar Gupta, involved in Case Crime No.11 of 2023 under sections 406, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 504, 506 I.P.C., P.S. Vikas Nagar, district Lucknow be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.

sentences.text: (iii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iv) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(v) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(vi) In case the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.
7.The application is allowed accordingly.
